business_scope.primary_industry_name: Retail Sale via Internet - DTC Brand Webstore

meta_jurisdiction_context.jurisdiction_name_en: Spain (Kingdom of Spain, national unitary jurisdiction)
meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Civil Law (codified continental legal system with sectoral elements derived from EU Law; commercial and corporate matters governed by the Spanish Companies Act and auxiliary commercial jurídicas)
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: Spain–Mexico DTA (1994, amended 2017) covering dividends, interest, royalties and permanent establishment definitions relevant to DTC e-commerce
Spain–Chile DTA (2004) including digital economy taxation protocols
Spain–Colombia DTA (2014) with PE thresholds relevant to Latin American DTC logistics hubs
Spain–Peru DTA (in force 2001) with reduced withholding for internet-based royalty revenue
Spain–Uruguay DTA (2012) covering dividend, interest and royalties and virtual-service income
Spain–Argentina bilateral investment treaty and DTA framework for reciprocal promotion and protection of investments
Spain–Brazil DTA (in force since 1980) as amended for royalties and technical service income
EU Trade Agreement with Andean countries (Colombia, Peru, Ecuador) covering e-commerce and intellectual property
EU Central America Association Agreement (commercial pillar) for trade with Panama, Costa Rica, Honduras, Nicaragua, El Salvador and Guatemala
EU–Chile Advanced Framework Agreement with digital trade provisions

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Ley 10/2010, de 28 de abril, de prevención del blanqueo de capitales y de la financiación del terrorismo; Real Decreto 304/2014, de 5 de mayo, Reglamento de la Ley 10/2010; Real Decreto 1582/2011, de 4 de noviembre, sobre Registro Mercantil Central; Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital, particularly Articles 33 to 36 on denominación social; SEPBLAC Circular 3/2018 and 6/2020 on UBO identification
ubo_and_aml_profiling.ubo_disclosure_level: Government_Only_Access (restricted UBO registry administered by the Registro Mercantil Central and the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública; accessible by competent authorities and obliged entities conducting AML/CDD, not open to unrestricted public search)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Negative Denomination (Certificación Negativa de Denominación Social)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) / Colegio de Registradores de España
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Domestic issuance by RMC; no apostille required when used in Spain, but apostille must be attached if the certificate is presented before a foreign authority under the 1961 Hague Convention

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized Deed of Incorporation (Escritura de Constitución de Sociedad Limitada)
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Spanish notary (Notario) authorized in the province of the registered address
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Notarial authentication; the deed is filed with the local Commercial Registry and does not require apostille for domestic use

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certified copy of foreign shareholders' passports, identity documents and corporate incumbency documentation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Consulary service of Spain in the source jurisdiction, or the competent authority of the foreign shareholder's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for nations party to the 1961 Convention; otherwise Consular Legalization by a Spanish Embassy or Consulate

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Power of Attorney for incorporation signing executed by non-resident directors or shareholders
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the foreign jurisdiction or Spanish Consulate in the foreign country
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (if the foreign jurisdiction is an Apostille State) OR Spanish Consular Legalization (for non-Apostille jurisdictions)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: UBO Declaration (Declaración de Titular Real) signed by every shareholder at or above 25% ultimate ownership
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Each relevant shareholder and the final beneficial owner before the incorporation notary
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Foreign signatures must be notarized and apostilled or consularized; domestic signatures are incorporated directly into the notarial deed

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory CDD/EDD under Law 10/2010 and FATF Recommendations. Every shareholder, director and ultimate beneficial owner must be screened against the consolidated European Union sanctions list, United Nations Security Council Consolidated List, OFAC SDN List, and Spanish SEPBLAC/CNMV internal lists. Enhanced due diligence is required where any UBO is a politically exposed person (PEP), whether domestic or foreign, and must include source-of-funds verification and senior management approval. Additional adverse-media and bankruptcy, money-laundering or terrorist-financing record checks are compulsory. For DTC e-commerce, the paying processor must be verified as a regulated payment institution and the company must not accept cash payments in its operational bank flow.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registro Mercantil Central (RMC) – Sede Electrónica del Colegio de Registradores de España (www.sede.registradores.org) and the CIRCE portal (Centro de Información y Red de Creación de Empresas, www.circe.es)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Company names must be expressed in Spanish or in any co-official Spanish language (Castilian, Catalan, Galician, Basque, Valencian). Names may only be transliterated into Latin characters. The denominación must not be misleading as to corporate type, must not be identical or substantially identical to any existing entity in the RMC database, and must not falsely imply a relationship with the State, the Royal House, territorial institutions, regulated professions, or financial activities. If the DTC brand name originates from a foreign script, it must be transliterated into a phonetic Spanish/Latin form and confirmed distinguishable in the RMC search system before reservation.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Ministerio, Consejo de Estado, Comunidad Autónoma, Embajada
Banco de España, Banco Central, bank, savings bank, insurance, reinsurance company
Real, Hispano, Nacional, Oficial (indicating royal or public prerogatives without authorization)
Sociedad Anónima, S.A., S.L., Sociedad Cooperativa (unless the actual corporate form matches)
Fundación, confederación, sindicato, corporación, órgano regulador (misleading institutional terms)
Abogado, auditor, gestor, corredor or other regulated profession unless the company actually holds the respective licence
Words that produce unfair advantage or trade-mark conflicts with an existing DTC brand in Spain
Expressions contrary to law, public order or morality
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: The RMC negative name certificate is valid for a statutory reservation window of 90 calendar days. No extension is granted by law; if the certificate expires, the proposed name returns to the availability pool and a new reservation must be requested. If the RMC rejects the proposed name, the applicant may file an appeal (recurso de alzada) before the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública (DGSJFP) within one month of notification, presenting this appeal under the Spanish Administrative Procedure Act (Ley 39/2015). Alternatively, the applicant may immediately reapply through the CIRCE/RMC portal with two or three alternative names. If rejection is based on trademark or confusing similarity grounds, a formal Spanish and EU trademark clearance report from OEPM or EUIPO is required before resubmission.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for a low-risk digital DTC brand store, provided the virtual office supplies a physical street address in Spain, not a PO Box, and is staffed during business hours for receipt of service of process and official correspondence. A registered agent or administrative office provider must maintain the company's corporate seal, statutory books and accounting records at that address. The Tax Agency (AEAT) will, however, require active management and control in Spain to treat the company as tax-resident; a virtual office alone is not enough for substantial economic activity when employees, directors or fulfilment activities are located outside Spain.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low-to-moderate for the e-commerce industry; estimated at 12–18% annual probability of an unannounced AEAT or Registro Mercantil documentary inspection during the first two years, increasing to 20–25% if employees are hired in Spain and subject to Social Security payroll visits. The company must keep the registered office address, accounting books, invoices, and corporate minutes fully available for inspection.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Company name reservation and issuance of negative denomination certificate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registro Mercantil Central / Colegio de Registradores de España
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Official statutory tariff of the Registro Mercantil Central, approximately EUR 12–22 depending on the number of name alternatives submitted

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Notarial deed of incorporation of an S.L., including bylaws drafting and legal corporate law review
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish notary (Notario) in the province of the registered address
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory notarial tariff; market benchmark for an S.L. incorporation is EUR 1,200–2,500 depending on deed length, capital and corporate clauses

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: UBO identification, ownership-chain piercing and PEP/sanctions screening software and external AML counsel
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: External Spanish AML/CFT law firm and compliance database providers
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark in the EU/Spain for a low-risk DTC entity with a single non-resident shareholder; range USD 850–1,200 per corporate structure

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Apostille / consular legalization of foreign shareholder passports, power of attorney and incumbency certificates
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Apostille competent authority in the source jurisdiction (court, foreign ministry or other designated authority) or Spanish consulate
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Per-document government fee of approximately USD 15–50 per apostille plus translation and courier costs; average USD 180 for four documents

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registration of the incorporation deed and legalisations with the Commercial Registry
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish Commercial Registry (Registro Mercantil) at the provincial level where the registered office is located
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory registry arancel charged on the nominal capital, number of registrable documents and the fiscal value of the deed

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual office physical address and registered agent service for the first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Registered office / virtual-office service provider in Madrid or Barcelona
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Prevailing market benchmark range of EUR 300–900 per year in Spain, depending on commercial district and the physical document-desk service level

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Corporate formation legal project management, incorporation filing through CIRCE, and administrative anchoring of the company
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Spanish corporate law attorney or gestor administrativo
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Common market fixed or hourly fee for an S.L. formation with international ownership chain, typically USD 1,000–1,800

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Real Decreto Legislativo 1/2010, de 2 de julio, por el que se aprueba el texto refundido de la Ley de Sociedades de Capital (LSC), arts. 4, 20-24, 33-34, 36-39, 58, 209-219.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial (Commercial Registry) of the province of the registered office; Registro Mercantil Central for the company name negative certification.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Escritura pública de constitución (notarial public incorporation deed) subsequently registered in the Registro Mercantil Provincial.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: SL minimum capital is EUR 3,000. The entire capital must be fully subscribed and paid at incorporation; a cash contribution must be deposited in a Spanish credit institution in the company name and the deposit certificate is blocked until registration. Non-cash contributions require an expert report under LSC arts. 67-73.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: Resolved, that the incorporators, having subscribed the entire share capital of EUR 3,000 divided into 3,000 ordinary equal shares of EUR 1.00 nominal value each, confirm that all shares are subscribed and fully paid in accordance with Article 22 of the Ley de Sociedades de Capital; Resolved, that the registered office is fixed at [street address], Spain, and the names of the designated manager(s) set out in the deed are accepted; Resolved, that [Name] and [Name] are hereby appointed as joint/solidary administrators with all legal and administrative powers; Resolved, that the administrators are authorised to execute the provisional tax identification certificate, social security registration, and all filings before the Registro Mercantil and Agencia Tributaria to complete incorporation.

step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Central (Central Commercial Registry), Madrid
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit an application for a negative name certificate (certificación negativa de denominación) with up to three proposed company names. The chosen name must include 'Sociedad de Responsabilidad Limitada' (SL) or its abbreviation. Upon completion, collect the certificate evidencing that the name is not identical or misleadingly similar to an existing registered name.
required_dossiers: Proposed corporate names in order of preference
Proof of payment of the official fee
Valid identification or notarial power for the applicant
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a name is refused as identical or contrary to law, submit amended alternative names; if the registry refuses the application, request reconsideration before the Registro Mercantil Central or appeal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Open provisional blocked bank account and deposit share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Spanish credit institution chosen by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of '[Company Name], S.L. en constitución' and deposit the minimum €3,000 share capital. Obtain a banker's certificate confirming the deposit and the blocking of funds until the company is registered.
required_dossiers: Bank account application and AML/KYC forms
Draft incorporation deed and shareholders' identities
Evidence of source of funds for the deposit
Description of business purpose and ownership
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank raises compliance questions, supply source-of-funds documentation and a clear corporate purpose; alternatively transfer to another Spanish credit institution and obtain a new deposit certificate.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execute the public incorporation deed before a Spanish notary
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (Notario) of the place chosen by the incorporators
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Appear before the notary with the name certificate, bank deposit certificate, and memorandum/articles of association. The notary verifies identities, records capital subscription and contribution, and grants the public incorporation deed. The deed is then used for the provisional NIF/CIF application and commercial registry filing.
required_dossiers: Passports/NIE and proof of address of all shareholders and appointed administrators
Notarial or certified powers if representation is used
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notary detects defects, amend the deed or supplementary documents; if a shareholder cannot appear, have the appearance performed by a notarially appointed legal representative or execute the deed in a new notary appointment.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Apply for provisional tax identification number (NIF/CIF) and Census registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) — provincial office or Sede Electrónica
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit Form 036 (censo de empresarios, profesionales y retenedores) using the deed data to obtain the provisional NIF for 'en constitución' legal entity. Keep with the deed and deliver to the registration file.
required_dossiers: Power of attorney or identification of the presenter
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If AEAT rejects the application, verify the deed data and resubmit; for missing documentation, present a certified copy and correct census information via the AEAT office.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Register the deed in the Commercial Registry and finalize incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial of the province of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the original public deed with the competent Commercial Registry. Registration is constitutive for the SL. After registration, obtain the definitive NIF certificate from AEAT, file the final Form 036 update, and if premises or employees exist, register the legal entity with the Seguridad Social (RETA) and the work centre.
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registrar returns the deed due to defects, remedy the defects through a complementary deed or correction, resubmit within the legal deadline, or appeal the refusal to the Dirección General de Seguridad Jurídica y Fe Pública.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable — no industrial manufacturing or extractive activity for ISIC 4791 DTC e-commerce; residual municipal licensing competence lies with the Ayuntamiento (city council) only if void offices/warehouses are opened.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: N/A for a pure Shopify DTC brand; a municipal 'licencia de apertura/actividad' may be required only for physical administrative or warehouse premises under local ordinances.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministerio para la Transición Ecológica y el Reto Demográfico (MITERD) and competent environmental department of the autonomous community
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt — ISIC 4791 and Shopify webstore operation are not listed in Annex I or II of Law 21/2013 on Environmental Impact Assessment; no EIA is triggered.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No industrial wastewater or VOC thresholds are triggered for pure e-commerce. If an office/warehouse is used, comply with municipal sanitary sewer discharge by-laws, the packaging waste management duty under Law 7/2022 on waste, and energy installations under the RITE (Real Decreto 1027/2007).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: For physical premises: obtain municipal occupancy licence, building usability certificate, and fire-safety clearance (boletín de instalación) before public access. Comply with the Ley 31/1995 occupational health and safety framework, including a risk-prevention assessment for employees. For a remote DTC operation without employees or premises, no civil defence certificate is required.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria (AEAT) – sede electrónica at sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es; administración competente in the jurisdictional province of the registered office (domicilio fiscal) of the SL.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: The SL is provisionally incorporated with a provisional NIF (código de identificación fiscal) and after deed of incorporation and inscription in the Registro Mercantil obtains the definitive NIF-number (Letter + 8 digits) issued by the AEAT via form 036/037. For foreign-owned entities, the resident director or appointed legal representative files form 036 before the AEAT for the definitive NIF certificate and simultaneous high censal; if the SL has no Spanish activity yet, a NIF de entidad no residente (same numbering series) is required, plus a VAT registration (NIF-IVA) when taxable transactions commence. There is no minimum capital requirement (Memorandum: capital fixed at incorporation, typically €3,000) and non-resident shareholding is permitted; however, if the foreign shareholder is a passive entity in a blacklisted jurisdiction (RDL 5/2023 anti-hybrid and DAC-6 transparency rules), additional substance evidence may be demanded.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation (Impuesto sobre Sociedades, IS) at 25% of worldwide taxable income; territorial limitations apply only to PE-like situations of non-residents; the SL is subject to corporate income tax in Spain regardless of distribution outside Spain; no pass-through regime exists for Spanish commercial companies.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: No check-the-box election exists under Spanish law. Available elections: (1) opt to be treated as a consolidated tax group under art. 58-70 LIS (relevant only for Spanish parent and ≥75% owned Spanish subsidiaries); (2) optional application of the OSS/OSS Union scheme for intra-EU distance sales under art. 73-79 LIVA (whereby Spanish VAT is not charged on EU consumer sales and VAT is settled in destination Member States when the election is exercised); (3) joint venture (UTE) election for a single project under art. 48 LIS with tax-neutrality; (4) tax transparency, hybrid mismatch and DAC-6 filing elections are not revocable instruments but mandatory compliance triggers under art. 15.7 LIS anti-hybrid rules.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: Value Added Tax (IVA – Impuesto sobre el Valor Añadido), governed by Ley 37/1992 (LIVA) and RD 1624/1992.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No registration threshold for businesses established in Spain: a Spanish SL must register for IVA with the AEAT (form 036/037) as soon as it conducts any economic activity, regardless of amount (even EUR 1 of turnover). For non-established suppliers of goods sold under distance selling, the applicability of Spanish VAT is triggered when intra-EU distance sales to final consumers exceed EUR 10,000 in the current or previous calendar year (unless the OSS election is made to tax in Spanish customers' Member States). For foreign e-commerce operators without a Spanish establishment, IVA registration is mandatory at the first supply of goods remote or through an electronic interface in Spain; the €10,000 threshold cannot be combined with a Spanish warehouse.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Spanish electronic invoicing is mandated for B2B invoices to all private and public companies under Ley Crea y Crece (Ley 18/2022), fully effective in 2025 for large enterprises and 2026 for SMBs; the verifactu standard (RD 1007/2023) now requires issuance of machine-readable invoices with an SHA-256 hash-chaining algorithm, secure transmission to a third-party or OSS system, and immediate delivery to the fiscal authority upon request. Supplementary obligation: the SII (Suministro Inmediato de Información) requires real-time transmission of VAT ledger data to AEAT in XML format within 4 business days (8 days for longer deadlines) for large entities with turnover > EUR 6 million and for those in the REDEME register; Shopify DTC brands below EUR 6 million fall under verifactu, not SII, but must still comply with the continuous-trail obligation (Trazabilidad de facturas) and maintain all e-invoicing records in the verifactu format; AC/AC and AC/NAC operation codes apply. There is no per-invoice government stamping or pre-clearance requirement, but AEAT may digitally validate invoices in real-time under SII, and foreign e-commerce operators must, as of 1 July 2021, obtain a specific NIF (NIF-IVA) and register under the Import One Stop Shop (IOSS) for B2C sales on imported goods below EUR 150.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating (exención con derecho a deducción) applies to: (1) definitive exports of goods dispatched or transported by the seller to destinations outside the EU (art. 21 LIVA); (2) intra-community supplies of goods (art. 25 LIVA) to a taxable person identified for VAT in another Member State, when the goods are dispatched to that member state; (3) services related to export goods (handling, transport, inspection, brokerage) under art. 22 LIVA when the underlying goods are exported; (4) certain intermediation services. For DTC e-commerce, a Spanish supplier shipping to a non-EU consumer at port of exit qualifies as a zero-rated export only if the goods physically leave the EU and the export is evidenced; services digitally supplied (e.g. e-books, software licences) are not export zero-rated — they fall under B2C supply of digital services taxed at customer location through OSS (11 H2 B2C) or under the non-Union OSS.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Customs Export Declaration (DAU – Documento Único Administrativo) accepted by the Spanish customs office (Aduanas) attesting national Union exit
Bill of Lading (maritime) or Air Waybill (air) or CMR carrier receipt (road) evidencing foreign consignee and definitive destination outside the EU
Commercial invoice showing the phrase 'Exención art. 21 LIVA – Exportación definitiva'
Inward Remittance Certificate or SWIFT/MT-103 proof of receipt of funds from the non-resident buyer into the Spanish bank account (bank certifying income of export proceeds)

Customs summary declaration (ENS) and EX-A/RSS if entry/exit through another member state (joint summary declaration), plus, where applicable, the 'exit report' (Informe de salida) issued by Aduanas through the SIGAG System
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: Spanish exporters must retain all export documentation for 4 years (6 where engaged in intra-EU supplies with evidence requirements); AEAT and EUROFISC customs-data exchanges trigger automatic cross-checks on zero-rated declarations. Frauds found to misapply zero-rating, including fabricated export documentation or non-arrival of goods outside the EU, result in: (i) a favourable assessment of the omitted Spanish VAT (21%) plus default interest for late payment (interés de demora, currently 4.0625% per annum); (ii) disciplinary sanctions under arts. 191-194 LGT of 50% to 100% of the tax evaded (grade: infringe grave if improperly claimed VAT exceeds EUR 3,000); (iii) proportional penalties on unsubmitted module 349/390 returns; (iv) retroactive clawback of input VAT credits erroneously sustained on export purchases; (v) criminal liability for tax fraud under arts. 305-305 bis Código Penal when the damage to the Hacienda exceeds EUR 120,000 per year — imprisonment of 1 to 5 years (increased to 2 to 6 years if using a company, or operating through corporate bodies with >50 employees up to 7 years). The limitation period for VAT recovery is 4 years from the end of the declaration period (art. 66 LGT).

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de España (Bank of Spain) in coordination with the Dirección General de Comercio Internacional e Inversiones (DGCI) under the Ministry of Industry, Trade and Tourism for foreign investment and trade-related FX reporting; the Ministry of Economic Affairs and Digital Transformation for capital movement oversight.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Spain maintains full convertibility for both current and capital account transactions as a member of the Eurozone and the EU. The euro is fully convertible; no exchange controls exist for residents or non-residents. Profit remittances are unrestricted, subject to standard corporate tax withholding (19% for non-resident dividends unless reduced by tax treaty) and compliance with anti-money laundering (AML) reporting. Capital account transactions (e.g., foreign direct investment, loans) require ex-post statistical declaration to the Bank of Spain for amounts exceeding €1,000,000, but no prior authorization is needed.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: No mandatory surrender or conversion of export proceeds is imposed. Spanish exporters may retain foreign currency in domestic or foreign bank accounts. However, all export transactions must be reported to the Bank of Spain for statistical purposes via the Declaración de Operaciones de Comercio Exterior (DOCE) within 30 days of the transaction, and the proceeds must be received within the legally agreed payment terms (typically 180 days for goods, extendable under certain conditions). No minimum conversion ratio applies.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account (Cuenta Corriente) and Capital Escrow Account (Cuenta de Depósito)
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account
Operational Account and Capital Escrow Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: Medium. Spanish law permits the use of Electronic Money Institutions (EMIs) and Payment Institutions (PIs) licensed in the EU (passporting) for cross-border payment services. However, for a corporate entity engaged in DTC e-commerce, a full commercial bank account is recommended for settlement of Shopify Payments, Stripe, and PayPal. EMIs like Wise, Revolut Business, or Payoneer can be used as auxiliary accounts for FX conversion and cross-border disbursements, but they may not provide full IBANs for all purposes and may have limitations on holding capital escrow. Legal constraints: EMIs are not credit institutions and cannot offer credit facilities; they are subject to AML/KYC under the same EU directives. For high-volume treasury operations, a tier-1 bank account is mandatory.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Physical presence is generally required for the initial onboarding of a corporate entity, especially for the legal representative (administrador) and any signatories. Most tier-1 banks mandate an in-person interview at a Spanish branch for the ultimate beneficial owner (UBO) and directors. Remote opening is possible for non-resident entities only if the bank has a dedicated international desk and the entity has a Spanish tax ID (NIF) and a registered address. However, due to enhanced AML scrutiny, physical presence is strongly recommended. For non-resident directors, a power of attorney (Poder) notarized and apostilled may be accepted, but the bank may still require a video call or a visit to a Spanish consulate.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-risk jurisdiction exposure (e.g., non-EU shareholders or beneficiaries from tax-haven jurisdictions)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Certified copies of passports and proof of residential address for all UBOs; (2) Bank references from the home country bank; (3) Source of wealth documentation (e.g., audited financial statements, tax returns, sale of assets); (4) Detailed business plan and expected transaction volumes; (5) Legal opinion from a Spanish attorney confirming the legitimacy of the corporate structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Unclear source of initial capital injection (e.g., shareholder loan vs. equity contribution)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Notarized and apostilled shareholder resolution detailing the capital contribution; (2) Bank statements showing the transfer from the shareholder's account; (3) Tax declaration (Modelo 200) or proof of tax residency of the shareholder; (4) If loan, a formal loan agreement with interest rate and repayment schedule; (5) Explanation of the economic rationale for the capital structure.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: E-commerce business with high cross-border payment volumes (Shopify, PayPal, Stripe) triggering enhanced due diligence
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Proof of domain registration and active website; (2) Shopify/PayPal/Stripe account statements showing transaction history and volumes; (3) Commercial contracts with suppliers and logistics providers; (4) VAT registration certificate (NIF-IVA) and proof of compliance with EU OSS scheme; (5) AML risk assessment and internal controls documentation.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident director or UBO without a Spanish tax ID (NIE)
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide: (1) Application for NIE (Form EX-15) and proof of appointment; (2) Notarized and apostilled power of attorney if the director is not physically present; (3) Proof of the director's good standing (e.g., police clearance certificate from country of residence); (4) Bank's internal KYC form completed with full details.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant wire transfer protocols: Inbound capital injections (equity or shareholder loans) must be routed via SWIFT MT103 with proper purpose codes. For equity contributions, use purpose code 'S001' (Direct investment) or 'S002' (Real estate investment) as per the Bank of Spain's Balance of Payments classification. For shareholder loans, use 'S003' (Loans) or 'S004' (Financial leasing). The transfer must include the company's NIF (Tax ID) and the concept 'Aportación de capital' or 'Préstamo de socio'. Verification: The bank will require the notarized deed of incorporation (Escritura de Constitución) and the certificate of the capital increase (Certificación de Acuerdo de Aumento de Capital) if applicable. For amounts above €1,000,000, the company must file the Declaración de Inversiones Exteriores (DIE) with the DGCI within 30 days. The bank will also perform a source-of-funds check.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Clearing rails for trade settlements: (1) SWIFT MT103 for direct wire transfers to suppliers, with purpose codes such as 'S101' for imports of goods or 'S102' for services. (2) Commercial Letters of Credit (LC) via SWIFT MT700 for high-value or first-time supplier relationships; Spanish banks issue LC under UCP 600. (3) For recurring payments to EU suppliers, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) is used, but for non-EU suppliers, SWIFT is mandatory. (4) For disbursements to Shopify, PayPal, and Stripe, these are typically settled via ACH or card networks, but the company must maintain sufficient euro liquidity in its operational account. All outbound payments must be reported to the Bank of Spain for statistical purposes if they exceed €50,000 per transaction (via the DOCE).
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forwards (deliverable) for EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and other major currencies, with tenors up to 12 months, available from tier-1 banks under ISDA or local master agreements.

Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for exotic currencies (e.g., Latin American currencies) where deliverability is restricted; these are permitted for hedging commercial exposures, subject to MiFID II suitability and reporting.
Currency Swaps (FX Swaps) for managing liquidity across currencies, typically used for short-term funding or rollover of forward positions.
FX Options (plain vanilla) for hedging downside risk while retaining upside, available from banks with derivatives authorization.
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) for long-term hedging of both FX and interest rate risk on foreign currency loans or investments.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual legalization of statutory accounting and corporate books (legalización de libros: Libro Diario, Libro de Inventarios y Cuentas Anuales, Libro de Actas, Libro Registro de Socios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial - Commercial Registry of the SL's registered address
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 4 months after fiscal year-end; calendar-year SL by April 30
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Books without legalization lose probative value in commercial litigation; registry may refuse to validate subsequent annual filings; persistent default contributes to 'hoja abierta' closure and can support administrative strike-off proceedings.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Deposit of Annual Accounts (depósito de cuentas anuales: balance sheet, income statement, statement of equity changes, notes, directors' report and audit report when applicable) presented in XBRL
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Registro Mercantil Provincial - Commercial Registry (electronic deposit portal)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within 1 month after approval by the shareholders' meeting; shareholders' meeting itself due within 6 months of year-end; calendar-year SL: approval by June 30, deposit by July 31
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Registry closure of the company's sheet ('hoja cerrada') blocking all further registrations until regularized; economic-administrative fine of EUR 1,000-EUR 2,000 per incorrect or omitted data item; non-deposit for consecutive fiscal years exposes the SL to administrative dissolution and strike-off from the Commercial Registry.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax return - Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades annual settlement including tax adjustments and carried tax credits)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT - Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within the 25 calendar days following the six-month post-year-end period; calendar-year SL: July 1-25
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing surcharges of 5%-20% of the outstanding liability plus statutory late-payment interest; penalty of 50%-150% of the tax shortfall for inaccurate returns; fixed fine from EUR 300 for failure to file; prolonged non-filing leads to enforced collection and registry-based corporate dissolution procedures.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual VAT recapitulation - Modelo 390 (annual summary of periodic VAT self-assessments; cross-border e-commerce B2B detail filed via Modelo 349 when required)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT - Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By January 30 of the year following the declaration period (calendar-year VAT)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Surcharge of 10%-20% of the amount due or fixed fine of EUR 300-EUR 6,000; repetitive omission is an inactivity red flag supporting AEAT requests for enforcement and strike-off of the registral sheet.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual third-party transactions statement - Modelo 347 (declaration of operations with clients and suppliers above EUR 3,005.06 aggregated per counterparty per year)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: AEAT - Agencia Estatal de Administración Tributaria, General Tax Directorate
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: January 1 - last business day of February of the immediately following year (calendar-year SL: February 28)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Fine of EUR 150 per omitted or materially inaccurate transaction (aggregate cap EUR 20,000); late filing penalty of EUR 300-EUR 6,000; systematic non-presentation is treated by AEAT as evidence of continuing non-compliance and may trigger registral strike-off intervention.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: A Spanish SL is exempt from mandatory independent audit when it satisfies at least two of the following three tests for two consecutive fiscal years: (i) balance-sheet total no greater than EUR 2,850,000; (ii) net annual turnover no greater than EUR 5,700,000; (iii) average number of employees no greater than 50. Statutory audit becomes compulsory when any two limits are exceeded; audits are also always mandatory for groups, public-interest and listed entities, credit/financial institutions and entities receiving significant State subsidies.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Individual statutory accounts are maintained under Spanish GAAP (Plan General de Contabilidad per Real Decreto 1514/2007 as amended by Real Decreto 1/2021), with the simplified PGC PYMES available for small entities; EU-endorsed IFRS may be applied to individual accounts and is mandatory for consolidated accounts of public-interest groups; the corporate tax base is derived from statutory accounting profit through the Impuesto sobre Sociedades adjustments in Modelo 200.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Beneficial-ownership confirmation is embedded in the annual accounts deposit: the Registro Mercantil deposit form requires identification of every ultimate beneficial owner (direct or indirect shareholding of or above 25%, or control by other means). Share transfers in an SL are effective against the company and third parties only after inscription in the Libro Registro de Socios and certification by the managing body; indirect transfers of beneficial ownership are disclosed in the next annual confirmation. The central Registro de Titularidades Reales (Ministry of Justice) is the official BO index for judicial and law-enforcement access and does not impose a routine annual fee.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro Registro de Socios)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas del Órgano de Administración)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 700 - USD 3,500 per annum (Spanish registered-address and registered-agent services for an SL, including receipt of official notifications, custody of statutory books and administrative support)
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 3,800 - USD 15,500 per annum for a small e-commerce SL under voluntary or threshold-driven audit (EUR 3,500 - EUR 14,000 at typical Spanish mid-tier audit rates)

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25.0% general rate for all resident Sociedades de Responsabilidad Limitada under Article 29.1 Ley 27/2014 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades).
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate for newly created SLs in the first two eligible tax periods on the first EUR 300,000 of positive tax base (excess at 25%); 60% partial exemption on qualifying IP income under the patent box regime (Art. 23 LIS); R&D tax credits of 25% base plus 42% incremental (Art. 35.1 LIS); 20% technological innovation credit (Art. 35.2 LIS); 10% tax-base reduction through the reserva de nivelación for entities with net turnover below EUR 10 million (Art. 105 LIS).
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Indefinite carryforward for tax periods beginning on or after 1 January 2015 with no statutory expiry; annual offset capped at 70% of pre-offset tax base for the smallest entities and reduced caps (50%/25%) for higher revenue tiers per Art. 26 LIS.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Modelo 200 (Impuesto sobre Sociedades) filed electronically through the Sede Electrónica de la AEAT (sede.agenciatributaria.gob.es) using a digital certificate or authorized representative; mandatory for all corporate taxpayers.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.reporting_frequency: Annual return supplemented by quarterly advance-payment instalments using Modelo 202.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within 25 calendar days following the six-month period after the fiscal year-end (Art. 136 LIS). For a calendar-year SL, filing window is 1-25 July; for a 30 June year-end, 1-25 December.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: NIF, fiscal year, form type and registered corporate address of the SL.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Auto-populated by AEAT; the NIF and corporate data must match the Registro Mercantil records; foreign shareholders are not declared in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Profit or loss before tax reflected in the statutory annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Gross up foreign-source income; reconcile with the balance sheet and profit-and-loss account delivered to the mercantile registry.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Increases and decreases to the accounting result: non-deductible expenses, timing differences, exempt income and permanent adjustments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a Shopify DTC brand, exclude income already taxed through a foreign permanent establishment and apply the DTA method of exemption/credit; TP corrections under Art. 18 LIS are entered here.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Tax base after offset of prior tax losses and the revenue-band absorption limits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Verify that intercompany purchases of goods from non-resident suppliers or payments to payment-service providers are booked at arm's length before the tax-base computation.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Applicable rate (25% general; 15% for new entities on the eligible tranche) and resulting cuota íntegra.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The 15% reduced rate applies only during the first two tax periods of substantive economic activity; a dormant or holding-only SL will not qualify.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Withholdings, instalments paid, tax credits and resulting amount due or refundable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach Modelo 216/123/193 certificates; foreign withholding suffered on overseas online-sales platforms is creditable up to the Spanish share of tax attributed.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing without AEAT notice triggers escalating surcharges of 5%, 10%, 15% or 20% depending on delay, plus late-payment interest (approx. 4.06% for 2025); fixed penalty of EUR 200 per omitted box or datum (Art. 198 LGT); substantive understatement triggers a penalty of 50%-100% of the omitted quota (Art. 191 LGT).
